pairs.subject: table
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:109 The event list declares a grid, but its gridcells never take focus (focus stays on the scroller, the subject link is tabIndex -1, and there is no aria-activedescendant), so a screen-reader user in application mode never hears the cell values J/K step through; separately, an order change remounts the whole Ledger, so no spoken status names the new sort.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:109 Grid role with one tab stop on the container; J/K/PgUp/Home/End move the selection only. No cell or row ever takes focus and nothing points aria-activedescendant at one, which is the 'cells that cannot take focus' anti-pattern. Home/End (Ledger.tsx edge) land on the last LOADED row while capped, and nothing says the landing is partial.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:92 The order is total and deterministic (kernel ORDER BY t, seq with seq as tiebreaker, events-query.ts:162). But the header button is not a columnheader and carries no aria-sort, and the change is never spoken: page.tsx:36 keys Ledger by order, so the aria-live Tally remounts as a new node instead of announcing the change.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:16 Keyset on the (t, seq) tuple with an identity tiebreaker; limit+1 gives the capped flag; 'older' is a load-more button; text-scan counts are written as `N+` with a 'searched N' chip.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:18 All-server: filter, order, window and counts are the kernel's. The two client-side figures (cost over loaded rows, the text scan) are marked '+' or page-local and not shown as totals.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/Toolbar.tsx:57 Free text is a draft committed on submit or Enter; facets and Seg commit on change into the URL (the applied predicate). Ledger is keyed by filter identity, so the rows, older pages and selection reset whenever the predicate changes.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:120 The server render settles before any empty state appears. Empties are typed by cause: nothing recorded, a partial scan ('0 in the newest N'), or filtered with a clear action. Navigations run inside a transition, so rendered rows are kept. Gap: a store failure (page.tsx ErrorLine) replaces the chrome and offers no retry.

app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:61 Pagination first (PAGE 500), then fixed-height windowing with heights taken from the tokens, and aria-rowindex on each row. aria-rowcount is the loaded count rather than the matching total.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/read.ts:34 Rows arrive in 500-row pages through an explicit 'older' press, so the spacer grows only by user action and stays far below the browser's scroll ceiling.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:88 The only copy is whole rows as JSON Lines (JSON escapes tabs and newlines). There is no cell-range copy and no paste.
app/(studio)/ledger/page.tsx:1 The ledger is read-only and append-only, with no editable cells.
app/(studio)/ledger/_ledger/List.tsx:84 The export is JSONL for agents and is built from the applied URL predicate. There is no CSV or spreadsheet consumer.

pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_library/Toolbar.tsx:82 Free-text search commits a server render 220 ms after typing pauses, which is the debounce-as-a-guess that the filtering technique names as the failure for round-trip commits; the rows follow a predicate the user has not finished stating.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_library/Toolbar.tsx:82 Every application is a server render (all-server regime), yet text commits on a typing pause rather than on an explicit act. Enter and ↓ also commit. Facets commit on click, and the draft resyncs from the URL (applied).
app/(studio)/library/_library/blocks.ts:6 All-server. Blocks are fetched by index into a sparse per-identity cache, and a stale response is dropped by identity.

packages/kernel/src/library/query.ts:31 Each order ends in the seq identity tiebreaker, and items without media (bad) have one declared home, last. Sort is a named Select whose value is spoken, held in the URL as identifying state.

packages/kernel/src/library/query.ts:22 Offset is chosen on purpose because the virtual scroller needs random access by index, and each order walks an index. Residual risk: a sync landing between block reads can shift later blocks.

app/(studio)/library/_library/Results.tsx:84 Unfetched blocks render as same-size slots under the chrome, with aria-busy. Empty appears only for a settled total of 0, typed filtered/unfiltered with a clear action. A block error is tracked separately from empty.
app/(studio)/library/_library/Results.tsx:48 Bounded block fetches plus windowing over the total, with options memoized on stable handlers.
